title: [YouPass Collect] - Japanese Salary and Television Price Trends
prompt: The graph shows the Japanese average monthly salary (Yen) from 1953 to 1983, and the prices of black-and-white televisions and color televisions during the same period. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The line graph illustrates changes in the average monthly salary in Japan and the prices of two types of televisions, namely black-and-white and color models, over a 30-year period from 1953 to 1983.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, while the prices of both television types exhibited a downward trend throughout the period, Japanese salaries showed the opposite pattern, rising steadily. Additionally, black-and-white televisions, which were initially the most expensive items, became the cheapest by the end of the period, whereas salaries, which started as the lowest figure, ended up being the highest.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding television prices, in 1953, a black-and-white TV cost approximately 110,000 yen, making it significantly more expensive than the average monthly salary at that time. Over the next three decades, this price declined dramatically, falling to 75,000 yen by 1958, then dropping further to around 40,000 yen in 1963 and continuing to decrease steadily, reaching approximately 20,000 yen in 1983. Similarly, color televisions, which first appeared in the data in 1963 at 100,000 yen, also experienced a considerable decline, dropping to 55,000 yen in 1973 before falling further to approximately 48,000 yen by the final year.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: In contrast, the average monthly salary in Japan demonstrated an upward trajectory throughout the entire period. Starting at 18,000 yen in 1953, salaries grew gradually to 23,000 yen by 1963 and continued rising to approximately 33,000 yen in 1973. The growth rate then accelerated significantly in the final decade, with salaries increasing to 50,000 yen in 1978 before reaching roughly 68,000 yen in 1983.
